expires_at.description: When the ask stops accepting a decision (ISO 8601).

decided_by_user_id.title: Decided By User Id
decided_by_user_id.description: Who approved or denied, once someone has.

decision_reason.title: Decision Reason
decision_reason.description: Optional note the decider left. Carried back to the bot on the wake — a denial with a reason is worth far more to an agent than a bare no.

viewer_may_decide.title: Viewer May Decide
viewer_may_decide.description: Whether the *requesting viewer* may **approve**: they hold the permission this kind requires and nothing in ``approve_blockers`` stands in the way. False renders the card without an enabled Approve button rather than one that would 403 on click. (Kept under its original name for shipped clients, which render read-only on False.)

viewer_may_deny.title: Viewer May Deny
viewer_may_deny.description: Whether the requesting viewer may **deny**: the kind's permission alone. Can be True while ``viewer_may_decide`` is False — a member who may refuse a request they lack the authority to grant (#3349).

approve_blockers.title: Approve Blockers
approve_blockers.description: Why this viewer may not approve, in words for the card; empty when nothing beyond the kind's permission is missing. Payload-dependent (e.g. the tools' authority, or the right to grant permissions).

requires_payment_method.title: Requires Payment Method
requires_payment_method.description: The organization is on its plan's card-free product variant and this ask is chargeable, so approving must collect a card first. The card routes Approve through the existing activation checkout and the grant is issued only on return.

blocked_by_plan_limit.title: Blocked By Plan Limit
blocked_by_plan_limit.description: The plan's hard cap for this meter is already reached. No approval can buy past a cap, so the card renders an upgrade CTA and no approve button — offering one would be a lie.

missing_permissions.title: Missing Permissions
missing_permissions.description: For a pending ``bot_tool.assign`` or ``permission.grant``: the permissions approving would grant the bot, each marked with whether this viewer can cover it. None for every other kind, for decided asks, and when not computed.

details.title: Details
details.description: Structured, kind-specific facts read from the stored payload — for ``permission.grant``, every requested permission — so a card can draw them as rows in every state, decided included. Server-derived from the payload the fingerprint binds, never bot-authored. None only when the stored payload no longer validates against its kind's schema; the card then falls back to ``spec.summary_lines``.

ApprovalRequestState.title: ApprovalRequestState
ApprovalRequestState.description:
Live state of an approval — the card's read model.

Served by ``GET …/approvals/{id}`` to every viewer with conversation access,
so the same card renders identically wherever it appears, including a
re-emitted duplicate lower in the same transcript.

ApprovalRequestStatus.title: ApprovalRequestStatus
ApprovalRequestStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a bot's request for a human's permission.

Unlike a question, an approval *is* single-decision: it authorizes one
action, so "has it been decided" is genuinely a property of the request and
lives on the row.

``PENDING``
  Awaiting a decision. Accepts exactly one, structurally — the transition is
  a conditional update on this column, so two people clicking Approve at
  once produce one grant, not two.
``APPROVED``
  A human said yes and a grant was issued. Not terminal: it becomes
  ``CONSUMED`` when the bot's retry spends the grant, which is the state the
  card renders as "done" rather than "waiting for the bot".
``CONSUMED``
  The grant was spent. Terminal, and the only status that proves the
  approved action actually happened.
``DENIED``
  A human said no. Terminal. Carries the decider's reason to the bot, which
  is worth far more to an agent than a bare refusal.
``EXPIRED``
  Nobody decided before ``expires_at``, or the grant was issued and went
  unspent. Terminal. Distinct from ``DENIED`` because no human declined
  anything — re-asking after an expiry is reasonable, re-asking after a
  denial is nagging.

is_mutation.title: Is Mutation
is_mutation.description: Whether holding it lets the bot change state. Only ``read`` is not a mutation; the card marks every other action so an approver sees at a glance whether they are handing out write access.

ApprovalRequestedPermission.title: ApprovalRequestedPermission
ApprovalRequestedPermission.description:
One permission a ``permission.grant`` ask names, as the card lists it (#4094).

The request as the bot made it, all of it — not, like
:class:`ApprovalMissingPermission`, the live remainder the bot still lacks.
A decided card has no remainder to show, but still has to say what was asked.

kind.description: Which registered action is being requested.

title.title: Title
title.description: Short headline — e.g. 'Create a hosted Grafana MCP server'.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: The bot's own words on why it wants this and what it will do with it. Bot-authored and shown verbatim; it is the part of the card that is actually an argument rather than a fact.

summary_lines.title: Summary Lines
summary_lines.description: The payload rendered for a human by the kind's presenter — e.g. the server name and container image. Server-rendered from the stored payload, not bot-authored, so the card cannot describe one action while the payload encodes another.

quote.description: Cost of approving, or None for a kind that spends nothing.

tools.title: Tools

ApprovalToolSummary.title: ApprovalToolSummary

Resolved from the catalogue at mint — as the *requesting bot*, so the card

with the rest of the ask. A slug the catalogue did not resolve still gets a
row (``tool_id``/``domain`` ``None``, ``name`` the raw slug): the card must
show everything the fingerprint binds, never a prettier subset.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description:
The identifier of the file, such as a unique ID.

This identifier can be provided to the model in a message to allow it to refer to this file in a tool call argument,
and the tool can look up the file in question by iterating over the message history and finding the matching `FileUrl`.

This identifier is only automatically passed to the model when the `FileUrl` is returned by a tool.
If you're passing the `FileUrl` as a user message, it's up to you to include a separate text part with the identifier,
e.g. "This is file <identifier>:" preceding the `FileUrl`.

It's also included in inline-text delimiters for providers that require inlining text documents, so the model can
distinguish multiple files.

AuthzGrantCreatedContent.title: AuthzGrantCreatedContent
AuthzGrantCreatedContent.description:
Typed content for a direct per-actor authorization grant being created.

A grant expands an actor's authority, so the record must answer "who gave
what to whom" without a join. Pattern axes are recorded as their canonical
strings, ``None`` meaning wildcard, matching
:class:`~botyard_core.authz.permissions.PermissionPattern`.

AuthzGrantRevokedContent.title: AuthzGrantRevokedContent
AuthzGrantRevokedContent.description: Typed content for a direct per-actor authorization grant being revoked.

AuthzMcpServerAccessChangedContent.title: AuthzMcpServerAccessChangedContent
AuthzMcpServerAccessChangedContent.description:
Typed content for an MCP server's org-level access mode changing.

Both ends are recorded rather than only the new value. "Set to restricted"
and "was already restricted" are different facts to an auditor
reconstructing when a server was reachable, and the route only emits this
when the two differ — so a reader can treat every record here as a real
transition rather than a no-op PATCH that happened to include the field.

``previous_access``/``access`` carry the enum's *values* (``open`` /
``restricted``) rather than its names, because those are what the API
contract and the UI speak; the column beneath them stores names, and
recording the storage spelling would make the trail read differently from
the surface that produced it.

AuthzRolePermissionAddedContent.title: AuthzRolePermissionAddedContent
AuthzRolePermissionAddedContent.description:
Typed content for a permission pattern being added to a role bundle.

Changing a role changes the authority of *everyone* who holds it, so this
carries the same weight as a direct grant.

AuthzRolePermissionRemovedContent.title: AuthzRolePermissionRemovedContent
AuthzRolePermissionRemovedContent.description:
Typed content for a permission pattern being removed from a role bundle.

Removal drops the role back toward the code-defined floor; it can never take
a built-in role below it.

BotChatReadiness.title: BotChatReadiness
BotChatReadiness.description:
Lightweight chat-readiness signal for a bot.

Surfaced to chat clients (widget/console) so they can tell an end user, at
mount and before any send, that the bot has no AI credential configured and
therefore cannot respond.

BotConfigUpdate.description: Request to update bot config via hot-reload.

avatar_url.title: Avatar Url
avatar_url.description: Avatar image URL — an image data URI (DiceBear SVG, or an uploaded WebP/PNG/JPEG) or an https:// URL. Max 16384 characters. Omit to inherit the source's avatar; send null for none.

copy_secret_policies.title: Copy Secret Policies
copy_secret_policies.description: Copy the source's Runtime Vault policy assignments, so the copy can read the same secrets. On by default because a copy that cannot reach its secrets is not a working copy; set false to start the new bot with no vault access. Only a bot owner can call this endpoint, and an owner can assign these policies directly, so this propagates no authority the caller lacks.

BotCopyRequest.title: BotCopyRequest
BotCopyRequest.description:
Request to copy an existing bot's definition into a new bot.

A copy duplicates what the source bot *is* — its config, managed workspace
files, skills, tools, tool domain settings, and credential assignments —
and never what it has *lived*: memory, conversations, disk, schedules,
devices, health, its email address, or its access list. The caller of the
copy becomes the new bot's sole owner.

skipped_private_credential_count.title: Skipped Private Credential Count
skipped_private_credential_count.description: Number of bot-private credentials on the source that were not copied. Private credentials are secret material owned by the source bot, so the copy starts without them and must be given its own before it can use those providers.

skipped_unavailable_tool_count.title: Skipped Unavailable Tool Count
skipped_unavailable_tool_count.description: Number of the source's tool assignments that were not copied because their catalog entry is no longer enabled or available to this organization. The copy has every tool it can still be given; these have no current equivalent to assign.

BotCopyResponse.title: BotCopyResponse
BotCopyResponse.description:
The created copy, plus what could not come with it.

Defined after :class:`BotResponse` because it embeds it.

avatar_url.description: Avatar image URL — an image data URI (DiceBear SVG, or an uploaded WebP/PNG/JPEG) or an https:// URL. Max 16384 characters.

description.description: Short human-facing description / role for the bot (e.g. 'Platform developer'). Display metadata only — not injected into the bot's system prompt.

credentials.description: Credential assignments to apply atomically with creation — the same body, validation, and bot-owner gate as `PUT /orgs/{org_id}/bots/{bot_slug}/credentials`. Model routing is derived from these links before the bot is first provisioned, so it boots on the chosen model instead of being reconfigured (and restarted) moments later. Any invalid assignment fails the whole create. Only credentials that already exist can be linked; a bot-private credential needs the bot first and is still assigned after creation.

Each value's `tool` discriminator must match its key.

BotCredentialAssign.description:

For each scope listed in ``scopes``, the ``credentials`` entries whose scope
matches are the complete desired state — existing rows for that scope are
removed and replaced. Scopes not in ``scopes`` are untouched. If ``scopes``
is omitted, the scopes are inferred from the ``credentials`` entries — with
an empty ``credentials`` that becomes a no-op, so set ``scopes`` explicitly
to clear a scope.

native_lane.description: How native owned mode treats this credential: the lane it serves it on, or why it refuses it (a native bot's chain must be all served). A fact about the credential, so it is set on every bot; the app shows it on native bots. Null unless the assignment is an LLM credential with an API protocol.

BotCredentialAssignmentResponse.description: A credential assigned to a bot.

BotCredentialReorder.description: Request to reorder credentials within a scope.

BotDeviceAssertionDeniedContent.title: BotDeviceAssertionDeniedContent
BotDeviceAssertionDeniedContent.description:
Typed content for a refused assertion exchange or session use.

``reason`` is the granular denial, which the *caller* is never told — the
API answers every refusal identically so the endpoint cannot be used as an
oracle for the registry's contents. The trail is where the distinction is
kept, because a human reading it later has context the endpoint does not.

``device_revoked`` is the reason worth alerting on: it means somebody is
still presenting the credential of a machine that was revoked, which is
the stolen-laptop signal.

BotDeviceCustodyTier.title: BotDeviceCustodyTier
BotDeviceCustodyTier.description:
Where a device *claims* to keep its private key.

*** SELF-DECLARED AND NON-SECURITY-BEARING. NEVER AN AUTHORIZATION
INPUT. ***

Useful for UX, inventory, support and org-level telemetry. Any
authorization that branches on this field is a **spoofable authorization
decision**, because the value is whatever the enrolling client said it
was. UI must render it as "reported by device", never as "verified".

The reasoning, which is the part that must survive:

* **macOS custody is definitively unattestable.** There is no public API
  to attest an arbitrary Secure Enclave key, and App Attest needs an
  App-Store-shaped bundle identity that a ``curl | sh`` CLI will never
  have.
* Windows and Linux with a TPM genuinely *can* prove custody — **and it
  does not help.** A tier ladder is only as attestable as its weakest
  rung: a client wishing to overstate its custody simply reports macOS +
  hardware, which we have nothing to check against. Attesting two of
  three platforms would not make the field trustworthy, it would make it
  *look* trustworthy, which is worse.
* Even complete attestation proves "this key lives in a genuine TPM",
  never "this host is not compromised".

A minimum-tier org policy is therefore an honour system, and must be sold
as one. The real control is that every use is server-mediated and
revocation is an immediate server-side deny checked on every assertion
exchange.

BotDeviceEffectCoverage.title: BotDeviceEffectCoverage
BotDeviceEffectCoverage.description:
How much of what a runtime does is actually mediated by Botyard.

Declared by the runtime and recorded per device. It exists so that a
clean effect ledger is never later misread as proof that nothing
happened.

A v0 external bot declares :attr:`PARTIAL`, and the reason is concrete:
the user's own Claude Code edits files and runs ``git push`` with zero
daemon involvement, so the platform observes a strict subset of that
bot's effects.

BotDeviceEnrolledContent.title: BotDeviceEnrolledContent
BotDeviceEnrolledContent.description:
Typed content for a device completing enrollment.

``custody_tier`` is recorded because it is useful for inventory and
support — **not** because it was checked. It is self-declared and carries
no security weight; see :class:`~botyard_core.models.enums.BotDeviceCustodyTier`.

BotDeviceEnrollmentTokenMintedContent.title: BotDeviceEnrollmentTokenMintedContent
BotDeviceEnrollmentTokenMintedContent.description:
Typed content for minting or regenerating an enrollment token.

``regenerated`` distinguishes the first mint from a replacement, and
``invalidated_token_count`` records how many previously live tokens the
mint killed — regeneration invalidates the prior token immediately, and
the audit trail should show that it happened rather than leaving a reader
to assume it.

The plaintext token appears nowhere in this content, for the same reason
it appears nowhere in the database.

BotDeviceEnrollmentTokenReplayedContent.title: BotDeviceEnrollmentTokenReplayedContent
BotDeviceEnrollmentTokenReplayedContent.description:
Typed content for a redemption attempt against a non-live token.

*** THIS IS THE SECURITY EVENT, AND ITS WHOLE POINT IS THAT WE CANNOT
TELL THE TWO CAUSES APART. *** Either the legitimate user re-ran the
installer, or somebody else is holding a token they should not have. No
field here resolves that ambiguity and none can — the event exists so a
human reading the trail can, with context we do not have.

``reason`` says *how* the token failed to be live, which is the part we do
know. ``presented_public_key`` is recorded because a replay presenting a
**different** key than the enrolled device is the strong signal: a user
re-running an installer normally presents the key they already have.

bot_id.title: Bot Id
bot_id.description: Bot this device is enrolled to run

public_key.title: Public Key
public_key.description: Base64url-encoded SPKI of the device's P-256 public key. A public key is not a secret; it is returned so an operator can match a registry entry against the machine in front of them

label.title: Label
label.description: Machine label reported by the device at enrollment

status.description: active or revoked

custody_tier.description: Where the device REPORTS it keeps its private key. Self-declared and never verified — UI must render it as 'reported by device' and must never present it as a verified property. It is not an input to any authorization decision

effect_coverage.description: How much of this runtime's activity Botyard mediates. v0 external runtimes declare 'partial'

enrolled_at.title: Enrolled At
enrolled_at.description: When this device redeemed its enrollment token

last_seen_at.title: Last Seen At
last_seen_at.description: Last time this device was observed. Liveness only; never gates validity

revoked_at.title: Revoked At
revoked_at.description: When this device was revoked; null while it is usable

BotDeviceResponse.title: BotDeviceResponse
BotDeviceResponse.description:
One enrolled device.

Note the absence of an expiry field: a device is valid until revoked, and
there is nothing to display about when it "runs out" because it does not.

BotDeviceRevokeRequest.title: BotDeviceRevokeRequest
BotDeviceRevokeRequest.description:
Devices to revoke.

A list rather than a path parameter, per the repo's batch convention: a
single-device revoke is a list with one entry.

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: State of each device after the revoke

revoked_count.title: Revoked Count
revoked_count.description: How many devices this call moved from active to revoked

BotDeviceRevokeResponse.title: BotDeviceRevokeResponse
BotDeviceRevokeResponse.description:
Result of a revoke.

``devices`` is the post-revocation state of each requested device. The bot
is deliberately absent from this response because revocation does not
touch it — the bot, its conversations and its history are unaffected.

BotDeviceRevokedContent.title: BotDeviceRevokedContent
BotDeviceRevokedContent.description:
Typed content for revoking a device.

Deliberately records that the bot survives: revocation targets a device,
and the bot, its conversations and its history are untouched.

BotDeviceStatus.title: BotDeviceStatus
BotDeviceStatus.description:
Lifecycle of one enrolled device.

Deliberately only two members. A device row comes into existence *at
redemption* — the row and its registered public key are written in the
same transaction that consumes the enrollment token — so a device is
``ACTIVE`` from the instant it exists. There is no moment at which a
device row is "pending".

What people mean by "pending" belongs to the **bot**, not the device: a
``self_hosted`` bot with a live enrollment token and no device row is
awaiting enrollment. That is *derived* from the absence of a device, not
stored on one, which is why no ``PENDING`` member exists here. A label no
code path can produce is read by every later maintainer as meaningful
state; adding a member later is one ``ALTER TYPE``, un-teaching a
misunderstood one is not.

BotEmailSentContent.title: BotEmailSentContent
BotEmailSentContent.description:
Typed content for a bot sending a single outbound email via Resend.

Emitted once per successful ``send_email`` MCP tool call. The enforced
``from_address`` is derived server-side from the bot/org identity — the
caller never supplies it — so it is recorded here for traceability.
Recipient addresses and the subject are retained for abuse investigation;
the email body is intentionally never stored. ``message_id`` is the Resend
message identifier returned by the provider.

bot_id.title: Bot Id
bot_id.description: Bot this token completes enrollment for

token.title: Token
token.description: The plaintext token, returned once and never again. Treat it as a live credential: whoever redeems it enrols their machine as this bot

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: When the token stops being redeemable. This expires the TOKEN — the bot survives and can be handed a fresh one

regenerated.title: Regenerated
regenerated.description: True when this mint superseded a previously live token, which was invalidated immediately

BotEnrollmentTokenResponse.title: BotEnrollmentTokenResponse
BotEnrollmentTokenResponse.description:
A freshly minted enrollment token.

*** ``token`` IS RETURNED EXACTLY ONCE AND IS NOT RECOVERABLE. *** Only a
hash is stored, so a caller that loses it must regenerate — which
invalidates this one.

BotFileSource.title: BotFileSource
BotFileSource.description:
What wrote a ``bot_files`` revision (bot catalogue D32, PlatDev #3684).

Lets later phases (D2/D17) tell a principal's edit apart from text a pack
wrote. *Who* the principal was is recorded separately in the actor columns
(``actor_user_id`` / ``actor_api_key_id`` / ``actor_bot_id``).

- ``USER`` — an edit by a principal: a person, an org API key, or a bot
  editing itself (MCP ``update_config`` / ``update_files``).
- ``PACK_INSTALL`` / ``PACK_UPDATE`` — a pack install or update wrote the
  file; ``pack_version_id`` is set (bot catalogue P2).
- ``PACK_UNINSTALL`` — uninstalling a pack restored the file it had
  replaced; ``pack_version_id`` names the version being removed (D11).
- ``ROLLOUT`` — a platform rollout rewrote it (bot catalogue P6).
- ``BACKFILL`` — the content already in place when provenance began,
  recorded by the migration or, for a bot that missed it, on first write.

NULL on rows written before provenance existed.

BotHarness.title: BotHarness
BotHarness.description:
Which agent software the bot runs.

Deliberately named *harness*, not *runtime*: ``runtime`` already carries
five unrelated meanings in this codebase (``Bot.runtime_class``, the bot
runtime image, ``ComponentName.RUNTIME``, Runtime Vault, and the
``bot_runtime`` audit domain), and *harness* is the vocabulary the native
runtime design already uses.

Distinct from :class:`BotType`, which discriminates the *shape of the
stored config blob* rather than naming the agent software. See
``Bot.harness`` for the full note.

Immutable once set, with one controlled exception: the audited, one-way
OpenClaw → native harness switch (PlatDev #3823). See ``Bot.harness``.

BotHarnessSwitchedContent.title: BotHarnessSwitchedContent
BotHarnessSwitchedContent.description:
The durable outcome of one OpenClaw → native harness switch (PlatDev #3823).

Records what the switch committed, so an incident can tell which model the
bot was routed to and how many conversations it left waiting for the L10b
reseed (PlatDev #2547), without reading the bot row as it is now.

BotHostingOptions.description:
The ``(hosting_type, harness)`` combinations a bot may be created with.

Exposed so the "Add bot" UI derives its options from the same allowlist the
API enforces against, instead of hardcoding the table a third time.

BotHostingType.title: BotHostingType
BotHostingType.description:
Who runs the bot's runtime.

Classical SaaS framing, with one caveat recorded so it does not drift:
"self-hosted" classically means the customer runs the *whole product*;
here they run only the **runtime**, while the control plane stays
Botyard's. The term is correct at the *bot* level ("this bot is hosted by
you") and must never be read as "self-hosted Botyard".

Immutable once set — see ``Bot.hosting_type``.

BotInboundMailboxPage.description: One page of a bot's received mail, plus the bot's own address.

hosting_type.description: Who runs this bot's runtime: hosted (Botyard) or self_hosted (the customer's own machine). Required, and deliberately without a default: a list that infers `hosted` from absence would label every external bot as Botyard-run, which is the exact gap this field exists to close. Note that it does **not** narrow `observed_state` — a self_hosted bot is provisioned a real Botyard-side runtime today, so it can read `running` while the customer's machine is shut. The two are separate subjects.

harness.description: Which agent software this bot runs: openclaw, claude_code, botyard_native. With `hosting_type` it is the bot's runtime profile, e.g. what a pack supports on it.

maintenance_restart_pending.description: True when a workload-aware maintenance restart is announced / in-flight for this bot (``bots.maintenance_restart`` is set). A pod-recreating update is queued but gated behind the maintenance engine (deferred to a window or waiting for the bot to go idle), so the bot keeps its old pod and stays running even though ``observed_state`` reads ``updating:infra``. UIs surface this as 'Running · update pending' rather than 'Provisioning'.

pending_config_changes.title: Pending Config Changes
pending_config_changes.description: Fields that differ between `desired_config` and the bot's last reconciled config (empty once reconciled_generation catches up to config_generation, or before the bot's first-ever reconcile, when there is nothing to diff against yet). Each entry's `path` is rooted at a top-level BotConfig field the bot detail page can edit (thinking_default, reasoning_default, system_prompt_mode, tool_search, heartbeat, skills, tools, model) — use the first path segment to route an entry to its owning card.

auto_retry_pending.title: Auto Retry Pending
auto_retry_pending.description: True when the bot is FAILED but the reconciler still has a retry scheduled for it (`retry_after` is in the future). Setup is not over: UIs should keep showing progress rather than a terminal 'setup failed' screen, which is what made a first-run bot look broken during a transient config-push error it recovered from a minute later. Goes false once the scheduled retry window has passed without the bot leaving FAILED.

A pod-recreating update is queued but gated behind the maintenance engine (deferred to a window or waiting for the bot to go idle), so the bot keeps its old pod and stays running even though ``observed_state`` reads ``updating:infra``. UIs surface this as 'Running · update pending' rather than 'Provisioning'.

BotRuntimeProcessExitedContent.title: BotRuntimeProcessExitedContent

BotRuntimeProcessWatchArmedContent.title: BotRuntimeProcessWatchArmedContent
BotRuntimeProcessWatchArmedContent.description:
Typed content for a ``watch_process`` arm attempt.

Recorded whether or not the arm succeeded, because a *refused* arm is the
more interesting record: it names a command a bot tried to run in its own
container and the reason the runtime would not run it.

``command`` is the shell string the bridge was asked to spawn, truncated but
never summarised — an audit trail that records "a command was run" without
recording which one answers no question anybody asks. It is absent for a
``pid`` attach, where there is no command to record and ``target_pid`` is
the whole of what was targeted.

BotRuntimeProcessWatchCancelledContent.title: BotRuntimeProcessWatchCancelledContent
BotRuntimeProcessWatchCancelledContent.description: Typed content for a bot withdrawing one of its own process watches.

BotRuntimeRestartRequestedContent.title: BotRuntimeRestartRequestedContent

BotRuntimeRestartedContent.title: BotRuntimeRestartedContent
BotRuntimeRestartedContent.description: Typed content for a bot runtime restart observation.

BotRuntimeScheduledCommandConfiguredCont.title: BotRuntimeScheduledCommandConfiguredContent
BotRuntimeScheduledCommandConfiguredCont.description:
Typed content for a command schedule being created or (re)configured.

A command schedule makes a bot run a shell command on a timer, unattended,
for as long as the schedule lives — so the trail records *which* command,
where, with which secrets (key paths only, never values), and which
conversation asked for it. ``command`` is truncated, never summarised, for
the same reason as :class:`BotRuntimeProcessWatchArmedContent`.

BotRuntimeServiceListResponse.title: BotRuntimeServiceListResponse

BotRuntimeSudoExecCalledContent.title: BotRuntimeSudoExecCalledContent
BotRuntimeSudoExecCalledContent.description: Typed content for a sudo_exec MCP tool call.

BotRuntimeToolCalledContent.title: BotRuntimeToolCalledContent
BotRuntimeToolCalledContent.description:
Typed content for any MCP tool call observed by the audit middleware.

Covers both first-party platform tools and external/BYO MCP tools.

``args_json`` / ``output_json`` hold the serialized tool arguments and result.
Both are ``None`` when the secrets scanner flagged a leased secret in the call
(all-or-nothing redaction — botyard-mcp never holds plaintext secrets to redact
in place) or when the scan could not run. Large outputs are head+tail truncated
(``output_truncated``); ``output_bytes`` always records the full, uncapped size.

BotRuntimeTrustTier.title: BotRuntimeTrustTier
BotRuntimeTrustTier.description:
The deployment shape a runtime was enrolled under.

*** NON-SECURITY-BEARING. NEVER AN AUTHORIZATION INPUT. ***

Recorded so credential eligibility, provider egress and support posture
have a seam to hang off later, and so a reader can tell what kind of host
a bot runs on without a live connection. It is emphatically **not** a
weaker platform principal: an external bot is a bot, and the tools it
calls execute in-cluster where the ordinary principal/permission model
already governs the decision. Branching platform-tool authorization on
this field would re-decide that, in the wrong place and by accident.

Two members, each produced by exactly one code path: ``USER_ATTACHED`` by
device-assertion exchange, ``CLUSTER`` by SVID exchange. The same reasoning
that kept ``PENDING`` off :class:`BotDeviceStatus` applies — no member
without a producer. Adding one is a single ``ALTER TYPE``; un-teaching a
misunderstood label is not.

BotRuntimeUserViewActAcceptedContent.title: BotRuntimeUserViewActAcceptedContent
BotRuntimeUserViewActAcceptedContent.description:
Typed content for a bot acting on the user's open Bot Page (#3298).

Emitted when the named user's tab claims an ``act_in_user_view`` batch,
which is the moment the actions leave the server for the page. The
envelope's ``conversation_id``, ``user_id`` and ``target_id`` (the exposure)
locate it; ``exposure_bot_id`` is the bot that asked and ``target_user_id``
the user it named, the sender of the turn it was running (#3323).
Metadata-only by design (epic #3238 slice 7, open question 1): the action
*kinds* and how many of each, never a typed value, selector, option or URL.

When ``executable_path`` is set, OpenClaw's plugin doesn't auto-infer headless from the binary name — it must be told explicitly via this flag. Default ``True`` because every Botyard bot pod is a server environment with no display.

BrowserConfig.title: BrowserConfig
BrowserConfig.description:
OpenClaw browser plugin configuration.

The browser plugin (powering ``mcp__openclaw__browser_*`` tools)
can launch a local Chromium-based browser or attach to a remote
CDP endpoint. Botyard ships the binary in the curated tools
component (``/components/tools/<ver>/playwright-browsers/``) and
installs a wrapper script at ``/home/openclaw/bin/chromium`` via
``bot/scripts/provision.sh``. The wrapper resolves the bundled
``chromium-<rev>/chrome-linux/chrome`` at exec time so the path
survives tools-component hot-upgrades that aren't coordinated with
a bridge redeploy (the curated tools layer can ship a different
chromium revision without rerunning provision). Pointing
``executable_path`` at the wrapper bypasses OpenClaw's discovery
cascade (Chrome → Brave → Edge → Chromium → Chrome Canary on PATH)
and avoids the bundled-revision-mismatch problem (OpenClaw vendors
a specific ``playwright-core`` whose ``browsers.json`` revision
may not match the nixpkgs-shipped one — explicit ``executable_path``
skips that revision check).

``no_sandbox=True`` is the right default for our deployment: every
bot pod is non-root with no ``CAP_SYS_ADMIN``, so Chromium's
sandbox can't initialise. Without ``--no-sandbox`` the browser
fails to start with a confusing error.

column_id.title: Column Id
column_id.description: Column id from the record_list field's columns, e.g. 'url'

CatalogFormRecordCell.title: CatalogFormRecordCell
CatalogFormRecordCell.description:
One cell of a record_list row: a column id and its value.

A list entry, not a ``{column_id: value}`` map, for the same reason as
:class:`CatalogFormAnswer` — a template may name a column ``token``.

cells.title: Cells

CatalogFormRecordRow.title: CatalogFormRecordRow
CatalogFormRecordRow.description: One row of a record_list answer.

CatalogueActionScopeResponse.title: CatalogueActionScopeResponse
CatalogueActionScopeResponse.description: One action across a whole domain, e.g. ``audit:*.read``.

CatalogueApprovedState.title: CatalogueApprovedState
CatalogueApprovedState.description: An admin approved it; a ``changed`` proposal's facts were applied.

current.description: The entry when the proposal was made

CatalogueChangedProposal.title: CatalogueChangedProposal
CatalogueChangedProposal.description: Upstream states different facts for an existing catalogue row.

CataloguePack.title: CataloguePack
CataloguePack.description: A pack in an org's catalogue, with its latest version's summary.

CataloguePermissionResponse.title: CataloguePermissionResponse
CataloguePermissionResponse.description:
One concrete, grantable permission.

All three axes are required, so a wildcard is **unrepresentable** here — the
schema, not a convention, keeps concrete permissions and open-ended scopes
apart.

CatalogueRejectedState.title: CatalogueRejectedState
CatalogueRejectedState.description: An admin rejected it; the entry was left as it was.

current.description: The entry when the proposal was made

CatalogueRemovedProposal.description: Upstream no longer lists an existing catalogue row.

CatalogueResourceScopeResponse.title: CatalogueResourceScopeResponse
CatalogueResourceScopeResponse.description: Every action on one resource, e.g. ``workforce:task.*``.

CatalogueSource.title: CatalogueSource
CatalogueSource.description:
Where a concrete permission was found.

Carried per entry because the two sources answer different product
questions: an ``API_ROUTE``-only permission is one a *user* can hold but no
tool can exercise, and a ``TOOL``-only one is the reverse. A UI that offers
"permissions needed by this bot's tools" needs to tell them apart.

CatalogueSupersededState.title: CatalogueSupersededState
CatalogueSupersededState.description: Upstream moved again before anyone decided; a later sync replaced it.

user.title: User
user.description: User ID from the Centrifugo connection token

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: Channel the client is subscribing to

result.title: Result
result.description: Empty dict on success, contains 'error' on failure

algorithm.title: Algorithm
algorithm.description: Hash algorithm the client must use (always SHA-256).

challenge.description: Hex-encoded target hash the client must reproduce.

maxNumber.title: Maxnumber
maxNumber.description: Upper bound of the search space.  Higher values increase difficulty.

signature.title: Signature
signature.description: HMAC signature for stateless server-side verification.

ChallengeResponse.title: ChallengeResponse
ChallengeResponse.description:
Altcha proof-of-work challenge returned to the client.

The client must find a number whose SHA-256 hash (combined with the salt)
matches the ``challenge`` value.  The HMAC ``signature`` allows the server
to verify the solution statelessly on submission.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: Chart data rows; each is an object keyed by ``x_key`` and every series ``key``.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: The queued message's request_id (from the chat send 202 ack / its assistant.queued event) to cancel before it runs.

status.title: Status
status.description: The cancel signal was forwarded to the bot.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: The queued message's request_id (from the chat send 202 ack / its assistant.queued event) to edit before it runs.

data.title: Data
data.description: The full replacement message content — a pydantic-ai ModelRequest, same shape the send endpoint accepts. Carries the edited text and/or attachments; it wholesale replaces the queued message's content.

status.title: Status
status.description: The edit was persisted and forwarded to the bot.

exposure_id.title: Exposure Id
exposure_id.description: The Bot Page exposure the context was observed in. The context is dropped unless this exposure belongs to the conversation's bot and organization and is not revoked or expired.

text.title: Text
text.description: Compact page context as plain text (at most 4,000 characters). Ignored when 'unchanged' is true.

unchanged.title: Unchanged
unchanged.description: True when the page has not changed since the previous message the client sent in this conversation; the bot is then told only that the page is unchanged.

ChatPageContext.title: ChatPageContext
ChatPageContext.description:
What the user's open Bot Page is showing, observed by the page script.

Everything here is untrusted: the page is the bot's own arbitrary code and
can report anything. The server treats it as data shown to that same bot,
never as instructions, and drops it unless the exposure belongs to the
conversation's bot.

ChatRequestMode.title: ChatRequestMode
ChatRequestMode.description:
How an inbound chat message is routed relative to an in-flight turn.

``queue`` (default) runs it in arrival order via the bot's inbound ordering
gate; ``steer`` injects it into the active turn. Mirrors the TS
``ChatRequestMode`` in bot/packages/botyard-channel.

client_request_id.title: Client Request Id
client_request_id.description: Idempotency key for this send, minted by the client once per message and reused on every retry of it. A send whose key this conversation has already accepted persists nothing and starts no turn: it returns the original send's ack (or, if that send failed or is still unconfirmed, the same error it produced). Guards against network-level replays, e.g. a browser retrying a POST whose connection dropped before the response arrived. Omit to keep non-idempotent behaviour.

mention_user_ids.title: Mention User Ids
mention_user_ids.description: Org members this message @-mentions; each is sent a notification anchored to this conversation, which clears when they reply in it or dismiss it. Duplicates are collapsed and the sender is ignored. All-or-nothing: the whole send (message included) is rejected unless the sender is a person, the conversation is shared with the organization, and every listed user can open it. The message text should carry the visible '@Name' itself; this list is what notifies.

page_context.description: What the user's open Bot Page is showing, when the chat is docked beside the bot's own page. Shown to the bot with this message only and never stored. Silently ignored unless the page belongs to this conversation's bot. A text over 4,000 characters is rejected.

ChatSendRequest.title: ChatSendRequest
ChatSendRequest.description:
Body of the chat send endpoint: the message plus an optional
idempotency key.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Request id for correlating this send with assistant realtime events.

ordinal.title: Ordinal
ordinal.description: Arrival ordinal assigned to the sender's persisted message — the send always persists it, so this is never null. The client stamps it on the optimistic bubble so it settles to its real server position immediately, without waiting for a realtime event.

turn_started.title: Turn Started
turn_started.description: Whether this send dispatched a bot turn. False when the send was answered without one — a native '/stop' or '/status', which the chat gateway resolves itself and whose result is already persisted and published as an ordinary message. No 'assistant.*' event will ever be emitted for such a send, so a client that renders a pending or streaming state on acceptance must clear it here rather than wait for a terminal event that is not coming.

ChatSendResponse.title: ChatSendResponse
ChatSendResponse.description:
202 ack returned by the chat send endpoint.

The ``request_id`` correlates the user's turn with the ``assistant.*``
events that flow over Centrifugo. In ``CHAT_STUB_MODE`` the API mints a
local request id and publishes the same assistant lifecycle directly.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: The queued message's request_id (from the chat send 202 ack / its assistant.queued event) to promote into the active turn.

status.title: Status
status.description: The steer signal was forwarded to the bot.

message.title: Message
message.description: Developer message text. Delivered to the bot's model as hidden system context ('[System message: ...]'); never rendered in the chat UI.

ChatWakeRequest.title: ChatWakeRequest
ChatWakeRequest.description:
Body for the wake endpoint — plain text, composed server-side into a
hidden developer message (clients cannot inject arbitrary message parts).

status.title: Status
status.description: 'waking' when a turn was dispatched; 'already_active' when the conversation already had a running or queued turn and nothing was sent.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Request id for correlating the woken turn with assistant realtime events. Only set when status is 'waking'.

selected.title: Selected
selected.description: The chosen option's key, or the reserved 'other' key when the respondent used the free-text escape hatch.

other_text.title: Other Text
other_text.description: The free-text answer, required when and only when 'other' was chosen.

ChoiceAnswer.title: ChoiceAnswer
ChoiceAnswer.description: An answer to a single-choice field.

key.description: Stable identifier for this field, used as the answer's key. Choose something meaningful ('ship_date') — it is what you will read in the wake.
key.title: Key

label.description: The question or prompt shown for this field.
label.title: Label

description.description: Optional elaboration shown under the label (context, constraints).
description.title: Description

required.description: Whether a respondent must answer this field before submitting.
required.title: Required

options.description: The options to choose between (at least two).
options.title: Options

allow_other.description: Offer a free-text 'something else' escape hatch alongside the options. Set this whenever your options might not cover the real answer — a respondent forced to pick a wrong option gives you wrong data.
allow_other.title: Allow Other

ChooseServerAction.title: ChooseServerAction
ChooseServerAction.description: Several of the org's servers fit: choose one (``complete_setups``).

ChosenModel.title: ChosenModel
ChosenModel.description: The request's ``credentials`` chose the bot's LLM; the pack's recommendation is unused.

provider.description: Provider the code may claim a tenant for

bot_id.title: Bot Id
bot_id.description: Bot that answers DMs in the claimed tenant; may be set later instead. A bot UUID, not a slug

ClaimCodeRequest.description: Mint a claim code for a provider tenant to redeem.

code.description: Paste this into the Teams chat to link the tenant

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: After this the code cannot be redeemed

ClaimCodeResponse.description:
A freshly minted code.

``code`` is returned **once and never again** — only its hash is stored, so
it cannot be re-read from anywhere. A caller that loses it mints another.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: Credential slug — used by the bridge to fetch a lease

key_path.description: Lease path the bridge resolves at exec time

ClaudeCodeCredentialEntry.title: ClaudeCodeCredentialEntry
ClaudeCodeCredentialEntry.description: One credential the bridge can present to the claude-code CLI.

credentials.description: Credential refs the bridge can lease at runtime

binary_path.description: On-pod absolute path to the claude CLI binary

can_self_wake.title: Can Self Wake
can_self_wake.description: Whether the bot can be woken when a process it started finishes — i.e. it holds the watch_process Botyard MCP tool. The bridge appends the watch tail to the background-task advisory only when this is True. Defaults False so a block persisted before this field existed still validates.

ClaudeCodeManagedEnv.title: ClaudeCodeManagedEnv
ClaudeCodeManagedEnv.description:
Structured ``claude_code`` block in the managed env payload.

Built by :func:`build_claude_code_managed_env` from a bot's config and
consumed by the bridge when serving claude-code lease requests. Plaintext
credentials never appear here — only slug / key_path / model references.

slug.description: Human-readable credential label, used by the bridge to key the token store

key_path.description: Dot-delimited secret key path, e.g. credentials.<uuid>.oauth_token

model.description: Claude CLI model ID (e.g. ``sonnet-4-6``, ``opus-4-7``). Free-form string — the FE picker constrains user input to the provider preset, and openclaw/claude pass unknown IDs through to the CLI.

binary_path.description: DEPRECATED — absolute path to the claude CLI binary on the bot pod. Ignored once the platform-owned CLI path is enabled: the executed command is derived from platform component state, not from this value. Retained only as the fallback for bots that predate the stable component symlink.

ClaudeCodeProviderEntry.title: ClaudeCodeProviderEntry
ClaudeCodeProviderEntry.description:
Claude Code CLI backend configuration for an openclaw bot.

Populated when a Claude Code credential is linked to the bot. Consumed by
the version-specific serializers to emit the CLI backend block, and by the
bridge to key the token store via ``slug``.

user_id.description: The person, as named in the request

connection_deleted.title: Connection Deleted
connection_deleted.description: Whether a Claude connection row was deleted

unattended_opt_ins_deleted.title: Unattended Opt Ins Deleted
unattended_opt_ins_deleted.description: Unattended opt-ins deleted, across every org

ClaudeConnectionErasure.title: ClaudeConnectionErasure
ClaudeConnectionErasure.description: What was erased for one person. Zeros when there was nothing to erase.

user_ids.title: User Ids
user_ids.description: Botyard user ids; each may appear once

ClaudeConnectionErasureRequest.description: The people whose Claude connections to erase, all or nothing.

ClaudeConnectionErasureResults.title: ClaudeConnectionErasureResults
ClaudeConnectionErasureResults.description: One result per requested person, in request order.

CliWatchdogConfig.title: CliWatchdogConfig
CliWatchdogConfig.description:
OpenClaw CLI watchdog overrides for the ``claude-cli`` backend.

Applied to ``cliBackends.claude-cli.reliability.watchdog`` by the
serializer. Both ``fresh`` (first turn of a session) and ``resume``
(every subsequent turn) profiles can be overridden independently.

Why we ship non-empty defaults: the upstream openclaw resume defaults
(``minMs=60_000``, ``maxMs=180_000``) are too tight for real bash
workloads — a single SQL query against a large table easily produces
no stdout for >3 minutes, and the watchdog kills the CLI mid-turn.
Our default raises ``maxMs`` to 15 min (900 s) so silent-but-progressing
tool calls don't get killed, while still detecting genuinely-stuck CLIs.

no_output_timeout_ms.title: No Output Timeout Ms
no_output_timeout_ms.description: Explicit no-output timeout in ms. When set, overrides the ratio/min/max computation. Capped by OpenClaw at ``timeoutMs - 1s``.

no_output_timeout_ratio.title: No Output Timeout Ratio
no_output_timeout_ratio.description: Fraction of the total turn ``timeoutMs`` used when ``no_output_timeout_ms`` is unset. Clamped to ``[0.05, 0.95]`` by OpenClaw.

min_ms.title: Min Ms
min_ms.description: Lower bound on the resolved no-output timeout (ms).

max_ms.title: Max Ms
max_ms.description: Upper bound on the resolved no-output timeout (ms).

CliWatchdogProfile.title: CliWatchdogProfile
CliWatchdogProfile.description:
One side of OpenClaw's CLI watchdog (fresh vs. resume turns).

Mirrors OpenClaw's per-turn-type watchdog override shape, applied to the
``cliBackends.<id>.reliability.watchdog.{fresh,resume}`` block by the
serializer.

OpenClaw resolves the per-turn no-output timeout via, roughly::

    noOutputTimeoutMs ?? clamp(timeoutMs * noOutputTimeoutRatio, minMs, maxMs)

capped by ``timeoutMs - 1s``. The upstream defaults (see
``cli-watchdog-defaults`` in the openclaw dist) put the **resume** cap at
180 s — that's the watchdog that fires when a single Bash tool call runs
silently for > 3 minutes (e.g. a Snowflake ``SELECT`` against a large
table) and SIGKILLs the whole CLI session mid-turn. Raising the cap is
the platform-level fix; bots can still override per-bot.

ClickAction.title: ClickAction
ClickAction.description: Click an element, as a pointer would.

runs.title: Runs
runs.description: 1-20 command schedules of this bot to run now. A schedule_id may appear once; a repeat rejects the whole request.

CommandRunTriggerRequest.title: CommandRunTriggerRequest
CommandRunTriggerRequest.description: Run command schedules now, each with optional allowlisted env overrides.

command.title: Command
command.description: Shell command to spawn. Do not redirect its output: the runtime captures stdout and stderr into log_path itself, and refuses a command that contains log_path.

cwd.title: Cwd
cwd.description: Working directory relative to the workspace root; omitted = the root.

timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds
timeout_seconds.description: Deadline per attempt; null means no deadline.

secret_env.title: Secret Env
secret_env.description: Env vars resolved from the Runtime Vault at each spawn. Names may not use the BOTYARD_ prefix: every run also gets BOTYARD_SCHEDULE_ID, BOTYARD_OCCURRENCE_AT (ISO-8601 UTC, the same for every attempt of an occurrence), BOTYARD_ATTEMPT (1-based), BOTYARD_RUN_ID and BOTYARD_TRIGGER (scheduled|manual). A runtime too old to carry them runs the command without any of them, so treat a missing BOTYARD_OCCURRENCE_AT as identity unavailable, not as a first attempt.

overridable_env.title: Overridable Env
overridable_env.description: Env var names a manual trigger (schedule_command_trigger) may set for one run. Empty = no overrides. Never a secret_env name or a reserved runtime name (BOTYARD_*, LD_*, PATH, HOME, ...). Override values are plain text stored in run history: never use them for secrets.

concurrency_group.title: Concurrency Group
concurrency_group.description: Lock shared across this bot's command schedules; omitted = no lock.

overlap_policy.description: When the lock is held: skip (record skipped_overlap) or queue (single pending slot, newest wins).

log_path.title: Log Path
log_path.description: Absolute path the runtime writes the command's stdout and stderr to.

output_path.title: Output Path
output_path.description: Absolute path named in the wake; never read by the platform.

exit_codes.title: Exit Codes
exit_codes.description: Exit code ('0'..'255' or '*') to success|failure|deferred. Codes not listed and without a '*' entry classify as failure. 'deferred' ("not ready yet, check again") needs a window, and a window needs at least one deferred code.

window.description: Run-until-success per period: rechecks a deferred exit every recheck_seconds until success or until the window closes (outcome 'late'). Omitted = every fire is a single attempt plus any retries.

on_outcome.title: On Outcome
on_outcome.description: Routing per outcome. Omitted: success and skipped_overlap do nothing; every other outcome wakes the bot and notifies the accountable human. 'deferred' cannot be routed (it is not final); 'late' needs a window.

CommandScheduleAction.title: CommandScheduleAction
CommandScheduleAction.description: Run a command on the bot's own runtime on every fire.

occurrence_at.title: Occurrence At
occurrence_at.description: The occurrence this run serves; for a manual run, when it was requested.

outcome.description: The latest attempt's raw outcome; null until it resolves.

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description: Run time of the final attempt (the successful one, for a success). Time spent waiting between attempts is not counted.

window_ends_at.title: Window Ends At
window_ends_at.description: When the occurrence's readiness window closes; null without a window.

next_check_at.title: Next Check At
next_check_at.description: While waiting: when the queued recheck or retry is due.

env_overrides.title: Env Overrides
env_overrides.description: Plain env a manual trigger set for this run.

CommandScheduleRun.title: CommandScheduleRun
CommandScheduleRun.description: One occurrence (or manual trigger) of a command schedule, attempts nested.

attempt.title: Attempt
attempt.description: 1 for the fire itself; 2.. for retries and rechecks.

outcome.description: How the attempt resolved; null until it has.

exit_code.title: Exit Code
exit_code.description: Process exit code, when one was observed.

not_before.title: Not Before
not_before.description: A queued attempt's earliest start (retry backoff or recheck time).

failure_retries.title: Failure Retries
failure_retries.description: Failure retries already used before this attempt.

log_tail.title: Log Tail
log_tail.description: Tail of the command's log, at most 8 KB.

error.title: Error
error.description: Why dispatch or resolution failed; the first 8192 characters.

error_chars.title: Error Chars
error_chars.description: Length of the stored error, in characters.

CommandScheduleRunAttempt.title: CommandScheduleRunAttempt
CommandScheduleRunAttempt.description: One attempt of a command run: the fire itself, a retry, or a recheck.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: Read it back with the schedule's command-run history.

occurrence_at.title: Occurrence At
occurrence_at.description: The trigger instant; the run's resume key.

CommandTriggerAccepted.title: CommandTriggerAccepted
CommandTriggerAccepted.description: A MANUAL run was queued; the scheduler-worker starts it within seconds.

holder_run_id.title: Holder Run Id
holder_run_id.description: The run holding (or queued for) the lock.

CommandTriggerAlreadyRunning.title: CommandTriggerAlreadyRunning
CommandTriggerAlreadyRunning.description: The schedule's concurrency_group is held; nothing was recorded.

env_overrides.title: Env Overrides
env_overrides.description: Plain env vars for this one run. Every name must be in the schedule's overridable_env. Values are stored and shown in run history: never put secrets here (use the schedule's secret_env). A bot whose runtime is too old to carry env refuses a run with overrides (outcome missed) rather than run it without them.

latch.title: Latch
latch.description: If this run succeeds, close the schedule's open run-until-success window: its pending rechecks for the current period never re-run. Only for schedules with a window. A failed or deferred run latches nothing.

CommandTriggerItem.title: CommandTriggerItem
CommandTriggerItem.description: One command schedule to run now.

CommandTriggerRejectReason.title: CommandTriggerRejectReason
CommandTriggerRejectReason.description: Why one manual command-schedule trigger item was refused.

CommandTriggerRejected.title: CommandTriggerRejected
CommandTriggerRejected.description: The item was refused; nothing was recorded.

duration_seconds.title: Duration Seconds
duration_seconds.description: How long after each period start rechecks may run, in seconds of local wall-clock time in the schedule's timezone: a 06:00 start with 43200 always closes at 18:00 local, across DST changes. Must close at or before the next period starts.

recheck_seconds.title: Recheck Seconds
recheck_seconds.description: Delay between a deferred exit and the next check of the same occurrence.

CommandWindow.title: CommandWindow
CommandWindow.description:
Run-until-success per period (PlatDev #4119).

The schedule's timing marks each period's *start*. A ``deferred`` exit
("not ready yet") queues a recheck of the same occurrence
``recheck_seconds`` later; a success closes the period; still deferring
when the window closes ends the period as ``late``.

CompactScheduleRun.title: CompactScheduleRun
CompactScheduleRun.description: One run on the status board's history strip.

reserve_tokens.title: Reserve Tokens
reserve_tokens.description: Token headroom reserved for reply generation and tool output after compaction. Derived per-model from the context window (``max(round(cw * 0.16), 16000)``); None omits the key so OpenClaw uses its built-in (16384). Omitted for native-compaction backends.

reserve_tokens_floor.title: Reserve Tokens Floor
reserve_tokens_floor.description: Minimum floor enforced for reserve_tokens in compaction paths (0 disables the floor guard). None omits the key.

mid_turn_precheck.title: Mid Turn Precheck
mid_turn_precheck.description: Run a context-pressure precheck after each tool result so a single large result triggers compaction mid-turn instead of overflowing the next model call. OpenClaw's built-in is off. None omits the key.

truncate_after_compaction.title: Truncate After Compaction
truncate_after_compaction.description: Rotate the active session transcript to a compacted successor after compaction so future turns load only the summary plus tail, bounding growth. OpenClaw's built-in is off. None omits the key.

max_active_transcript_bytes.title: Max Active Transcript Bytes
max_active_transcript_bytes.description: Trigger proactive local compaction when the active transcript reaches this byte size, independent of (unreliable) token estimates. Derived per-model as ``context_window * 40`` (~40 bytes/token for tool-heavy bots). None omits the key.

timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds
timeout_seconds.description: Maximum wall-clock seconds allowed for one local compaction operation. Botyard defaults to 10 minutes because large history summaries can legitimately exceed OpenClaw's shorter runtime default. Global (not per-model); always emitted.

CompactionConfig.title: CompactionConfig
CompactionConfig.description:
Context-compaction safeguards serialized into the openclaw config.

Defaults harden bots against the overflow -> failed-compaction ->
stuck-session-write-lock trap (upstream openclaw #699 / #70334). Only
serializers whose schema exposes these keys emit them (v2026.6.1+);
older versions ignore the fields.

The token-budget knobs are ``| None`` so the builder can OMIT them for a bot
whose primary model is routed through a backend that owns native compaction
(claude-cli, Codex harness), where they are inert. The concrete field
defaults reproduce the historical 200k-window derivation, so a config built
without the credential-driven resolution still emits sane safeguards.
``timeout_seconds`` stays a non-optional global (a compaction-operation
wall-clock cap, not a per-model attribute) and is always emitted.

reserve_tokens.title: Reserve Tokens
reserve_tokens.description: Reply/tool headroom tokens reserved after compaction.

mid_turn_precheck.title: Mid Turn Precheck
mid_turn_precheck.description: Run a tool-loop context precheck before the next model call.

truncate_after_compaction.title: Truncate After Compaction
truncate_after_compaction.description: Rotate the active transcript to a compacted successor.

max_active_transcript_bytes.title: Max Active Transcript Bytes
max_active_transcript_bytes.description: Byte size that triggers proactive local compaction.

timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds
timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds allowed for one compaction operation.

CompactionConfigPatch.title: CompactionConfigPatch
CompactionConfigPatch.description: Patchable compaction fields (all optional; only provided fields apply).

CompactionPart.title: CompactionPart
CompactionPart.description:
A compaction part that summarizes previous conversation history.

Compaction parts contain an opaque or readable summary of prior messages,
produced by provider-specific compaction mechanisms. They must be round-tripped
back to the same provider in subsequent requests.

For Anthropic, `content` contains a readable text summary.
For OpenAI, `content` is `None` and the encrypted data is stored in `provider_details`.

CompatiblePresetModelResponse.description: A model exposed by a credential preset for OpenClaw routing.

ComponentDeploymentHealth.description: Normalized health of one component on one reconciliation target.

deployment_id.description: Stable composite identifier for this component target

catalog_slug.description: Source MCP catalogue slug, when applicable

observed_artifact.description: Durably observed running artifact; null when the reconciler does not persist it

ComponentDeploymentResponse.description: Desired and observed evidence for one component on one target.

ComponentName.title: ComponentName
ComponentName.description: Bot component identifiers, delivered as payloads or runnable images.

keep.description: Versions that will be kept (in-use, default, recent, rollback buffer)

prune.description: Versions selected for removal from disk

status.description: ``pending`` until the customer finishes; then ``connected`` (the tile exists), ``expired`` (the deadline passed or the customer cancelled), or ``failed`` (the vendor reported a terminal failure). ``needs_reauth`` is the one that is neither: the tile exists and is installed, and the customer's authorisation stopped working afterwards — most often because they revoked Botyard in their own Google or Slack settings.
